messages:
mira: Starting canary rollout v2.4.1 -> canary-pool at 10%.
mira: Kicking off rapid telemetry quickscan (healthscan + kv-ttl-check + prefill-watch). Tagging @sam @jon for ops.
deploy-bot: DEPLOYBOT: quickscan started · checks: healthscan:ok kv-ttl-check:monitoring prefill-watch:pending · results will stream here
sam: Raw telemetry looks noisy. p95 for kv-ttl-check jumped from 120ms -> 1.2s in apac1 around 02:15 UTC.
sam: Logs show repeated backend timeout fetching prefix and TTL misses. Suspect prefill race on new model variant.
jon: Can we pause ramp? Recommend keep at 10% and increase quickscan frequency to 30s for 10m. If failures persist, rollback to v2.4.0.
mira: Pausing automatic ramp. Increasing quickscan cadence now.
mira: Running quick prefill against canary instances: `curl -sS https://canary.internal/warmup -X POST -d '{\'prefixes\':5}'`
lee: Observed warmup echo: prefill_ok=true ttl_missed=0 on 3 of 4 canary pods; one pod still showing ttl_missed=2.
deploy-bot: quickscan update · kv-ttl-check: failure_rate 0.03 -> 0.01 p95 1.2s -> 420ms · warmup success:3/4 · sampling_rate increased to 30s
jon: That improvement is encouraging but p95 still elevated. I'm going to push a tiny hotfix (increase cache TTL on canary only) and re-run warmup.
mira: Sounds good. If hotfix doesn't reduce p95 below 300ms in 10m we rollback. @sam keep the release window open for 30m.
sam: Ack. I'll prepare rollback command and monitor dashboards.
jon: Rollback command ready: `deployctl rollback --to v2.4.0 --selector canary=true` (will keep telemetry tags)
mira: Thanks. Will update when hotfix lands. :eyes:
